coupling.rationale: Exemplary server/client separation with typed DTO seams, explicit URL-query state, and props-only components. Two tangles keep it below 5: the display-name rule is split between server-provided labels and client-side humanize() calls, and the API base URL is known by both a server util and a client component.

app/app/components/TypeBadge.vue:4-9 — link optional via a single flag, no flag creep

abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's real variation well (cards with optional hidden/types, sections, type badges, sortable tables) and a new resource type reuses nearly all helpers. Two copy-paste seams — the home-page grid and the facts dl — plus the missing shared layout for site chrome keep it from 5.

findings.issue: Site header/footer markup duplicated from app/app/app.vue:5-14, using plain <a> instead of NuxtLink; any nav, footer or chrome change must be made twice and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Move the chrome into layouts/default.vue (or a SiteChrome component) and render <NuxtLayout> from both app.vue and error.vue, as the Nuxt docs recommend.

findings.issue: Home page inlines the card-grid ul/li instead of using CardList because CardList doesn't pass through the types badges, so list-wide changes (sorting, markup, a11y) need two edits.
findings.suggestion: Let CardList accept an optional types passthrough (Card already carries display data; extend Card/IndexEntry or add a showTypes variant) and use CardList here too.

findings.issue: Display-name rule split across layers: server DTOs precompute labels (e.g. MoveData.label, TypeRef) but abilities and evolution links are humanized on the client (also app/app/components/EvolutionTree.vue:10, PokemonCard.vue:12).
findings.suggestion: Have the PokemonData DTO carry English/humanized labels for abilities and evolution nodes, keeping name-shaping rules in one layer.

findings.issue: Client component re-derives the API base URL and hardcodes the media sprite path, duplicating knowledge that lives in server/utils/pokeapi.ts (and diverging from the artwork URL already provided by the Pokemon DTO).
findings.suggestion: Provide the sprite URL (or pokemon id + media base helper) through the Card DTO, or add a shared/utils media helper so the URL scheme has one home.

findings.issue: The 'facts' description list is hand-rolled and structurally duplicated in app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:52-60; an Items section shaped like Moves would copy it a third time.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small FactsList (or DefList) component taking term/value pairs.

findings.issue: The index DTO is assembled via reverse mapping (types endpoint → pokemon lists, generations endpoint → species) rather than the speciesCards/default-pokemon path used elsewhere, so Pokémon↔species↔type fixes can land in two data paths.
findings.suggestion: Consider sharing the default-pokemon/type mapping helpers in server/utils/data.ts so both paths share one source of truth.

summary: This is a cleanly layered Nuxt 4 app: raw PokeAPI knowledge is confined to server utils, DTOs in shared/types are the narrow contract, and pages/components are thin and props-driven, so almost any change lands in one obvious place. The deductions are a handful of duplication seams — the site chrome exists in both app.vue and error.vue, the home page re-implements the CardList grid and its own data assembly, and the display-name/URL rules are split between server and client. All are easy fixes; nothing is entangled.
